observation_summary: The continued fraction evaluation in the Beta distribution calculation diverges to NaN or infinity for large parameters, causing failures in cumulative probability calculations for Binomial and F distributions.
hypothesis: The original implementation of the continued fraction evaluation was numerically unstable for large inputs, leading to overflow or NaN results. The fix replaces the unstable recurrence relation with a more robust version that includes scaling/normalization to prevent divergence.
prediction: The code will show a complete rewrite of the recurrence relation logic inside the ContinuedFraction.evaluate method, replacing the previous variables (p0, q1, q2, cN) with a new, more stable iterative approach.
experiment_rationale: The diff shows a complete overhaul of the iterative computation logic within the ContinuedFraction class. The removal of complex scaling logic and the introduction of a simpler, more stable recurrence relation (dN, cN) confirms that the underlying computational procedure was flawed.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic numerical stability issue in a mathematical algorithm. The fix involves rewriting the core iterative procedure used to evaluate the continued fraction. This is not a missing check (Checking), a simple value assignment (Assignment/Initialization), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object). It is a fundamental correction to the computational method used to approximate the function.
evidence_used: The diff shows a complete rewrite of the loop body in ContinuedFraction.java.
The bug report mentions 'Continued fraction diverged to NaN'.
The fix replaces the previous recurrence variables (p0, q1, q2, cN) with a new set (dN, cN) and updates the iteration logic.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the code does have checks for infinity/NaN, the root cause is the instability of the algorithm itself, not the lack of a guard.
The fix is not just changing a constant or initialization, but rewriting the entire iterative computational procedure.
